title: Arise and warn
hookLine: O you cloaked, arise, magnify your Lord, purify your garments (74:1–4)

cards: After the first revelation in the cave, the tradition says, the visits stopped for a while. Then one day, walking, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ heard a voice and looked up.
The same angel he'd seen in the cave was there, seated between sky and earth. He ran home shaking and said to his family: cover me, cover me. They wrapped him in a cloak.
And under the cloak, the next words came. Surah seventy-four, al-Muddaththir, the one cloaked.

teach.b: The surah opens, in Pickthall's translation: "O thou enveloped in thy cloak, Arise and warn! Thy Lord magnify, Thy raiment purify." The story of the cloak is in Sahih al-Bukhari, from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah.
Jabir thought this surah was the very first revelation; others, following 'A'ishah's account of the cave, also in al-Bukhari, say al-'Alaq came first, and al-Muddaththir after the pause.
Either way, these are the words that turned a private experience into a public mission. Four commands. Qum: arise, get out from under the cloak.
Fa-andhir: and warn, tell people what's coming.

Wa rabbaka fa-kabbir: and your Lord, magnify, the same root as Allahu akbar, God is greater. Before you warn anyone, set Allah above everything, including your own fear. And thiyabaka fa-tahhir: your garments, purify.
Here the commentators split. Some read it literally: keep your clothes clean, especially for prayer.

Others read garments as a picture of the self: purify your deeds, your heart, your intentions. Some hold that both meanings are meant, the outer and the inner together. Then verse five adds: and shun what is foul.
Get up. Speak. Make Allah great in your eyes.
Clean yourself, inside and out. It's a morning routine for someone about to face a hostile city. The Prophet had just said cover me.
The answer was: arise. Not a rebuke. A job, and the dignity that comes with being given one.

how: Muslims pray in clean clothes on a clean place, and commentators read 74:4 as calling for purity of both garments and heart; the surah is remembered as the call that began the Prophet's public mission.

o: the messenger angel, wrapped in light
the one cloaked, told to arise and warn
the one who stays hidden, praying alone

games.q: arise and warn — tap the pairs.
p: magnify: the root of Allahu akbar

s: all scholars agree al-Muddaththir was the first revelation
Jabir thought so; others, following 'A'ishah's account, say al-'Alaq came first.
commentators read 'purify your garments' in more than one way
literally, clothes; or the heart and deeds; some say both.
the call to arise came as a rebuke

games.q: you've just seen the angel between sky and earth. you run home shaking: cover me. what comes next?
games.why: o you cloaked, arise and warn, magnify your Lord, purify your garments. the private experience became a public mission.

practice: Sit up straight and tend to what you're wearing: smooth a sleeve, straighten a collar, brush something off your knee, slowly, as if getting ready for something important.
Then do the same inside, and notice one thing in your heart you'd like to wash out today, a grudge, a lie, a bad mood.

wordCard.voice: Al-Muddaththir. The one cloaked: in 74:1–4 the Prophet, wrapped under his cloak, is told to arise, warn, magnify his Lord, and purify his garments. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: arise. Under the cloak is not where the story ends. Day six hundred fifty-five, and counting.
